opEmptyTitle: No recent strategy judgment for now
opEmptyConclusion: The 3-week window has no visible collection, so it is not used to judge that brands stopped sending or that themes have changed.
opEmptyAction: First verify the site and collection coverage, then look for leads worth validating in the 3-month data in the appendix.
opEmptyWatchOld: Three-month records cannot substitute for recent evidence from the 3-week window.
opEmptyWatchCutoff: The query is fixed as of {date}; that does not mean nothing was sent after it.
opEmptyNext: Do not adjust theme budgets or sending frequency until the recent sample is filled in.
opD1Title: Who to look at first: choose the review targets
opD1ConclusionOne: {brands} is the brand with the most collected emails in the current visible sample; use it first as an entry point for creative review, not as an effectiveness benchmark.
opD1ConclusionTie: {brands} are tied as the brands with the most collected emails in the current visible sample; use them first as entry points for creative review, not as effectiveness benchmarks.
opEvidence: {count} {count, plural, one {email} other {emails}}, {pct}% of the 3-week sample.
opEvidenceEach: {count} {count, plural, one {email} other {emails}} each, {pct}% of the 3-week sample.
opD1Action: First pick representative emails from that brand on the same theme and compare the benefit points, the CTA and the landing page; avoid mixing emails with different jobs.
opD2Title: What to look at: form a content hypothesis
opD2ConclusionOne: {themes} is the most collected theme and can be a starting point for content exploration, but user preference cannot be asserted from this alone.
opD2ConclusionTie: {themes} are tied as the most collected themes and can be a starting point for content exploration, but user preference cannot be asserted from this alone.
opD2ActionMulti: First sample and compare the content and audiences of the tied themes, pick one hypothesis for a single-variable test, and do not force a bet on a single theme based on the ranking.
opD2ActionPrice: First break down the consistency across discount thresholds, benefit framing and the landing page; test with your own sample and do not simply match prices.
opD2ActionOther: First separate service, legal and marketable content; do not turn the 'other' collection volume into a marketing schedule.
opD2ActionTheme: First sample and review how {theme} expresses its value and how the landing page carries it, then verify whether it fits your own audience.
opD3Title: When to look: check the outreach cadence
opD3ConclusionFlat: The daily collected volume is the same in every week, with no clear cadence peak; check content differences first instead of inventing a reason to send more often.
opD3ConclusionPeak: {weeks} recorded the highest average daily visible collection, which is worth cross-checking against campaign moments and notification emails.
opD3Evidence: Normalized by the actual days in each bucket: {parts}.
opD3Action: Treat high-frequency periods as leads to verify; test frequency changes on your own comparable audience first, while watching unsubscribes and conversions, and do not copy competitor frequency.
opWatchSmall: The recent sample is small, so a few new records could change the ranking; gather more evidence first and avoid strong attribution.
opWatchOther: The 'other' category holds {count} {count, plural, one {email} other {emails}}, which may include service or legal notices; confirm their purpose before including them in marketing benchmarks.
opWatchMarket: The sample comes from visible collection in {market}; collection coverage differs by market, so absolute email volume must not be treated as market demand or an effectiveness ranking.
opWatchCutoff: The query is fixed as of {date}; the 3-week and 3-month windows are different windows, and their totals cannot be read directly as growth.
opWatchNoMetrics: There are no open-rate, click-rate, conversion or unsubscribe data; the conclusions below are for setting review and experiment priorities and do not prove marketing effectiveness.
opNextStep: This round, choose only one content or cadence hypothesis; first verify the purpose and creative of the emails, then run a single-variable test on a comparable audience, and decide whether to expand based on conversion and unsubscribe feedback.
opScopeLine: **Scope**: 3-week {range}, {total} {total, plural, one {email} other {emails}}; 3-month {range3}, {count} {count, plural, one {email} other {emails}}. The query is fixed as of {date}; it is not an open-ended date query.
opScopeNote: Counts are Milled's visibly collected emails, not actual total sends. Each email is assigned to exactly one theme; service and legal notices are included, so not all of them can be called marketing. There are no open, click or conversion rates, so marketing effectiveness is not inferred from them.
opQ1Title: 1. What has the current site been doing recently?
opQ2Title: 2. How do themes and brands differ in daily frequency?
opQ3Title: 3. Which keywords are labeled on the current site?
opNoKeywords: The current site has no valid keyword labels yet. An empty field does not mean the email bodies contain no keywords.
opQ4Title: 4. How should this be verified next?
opVerify1: Use the current site's themes and weekly distribution as exploration leads; first separate marketing content from service and legal notices, then design single-variable tests for a comparable audience.
opVerify2: Sending frequency should be tested against your own users' intent and unsubscribe feedback; do not treat competitors' visibly collected volume as a sending target.
opVerify3: All copy and banner approaches still require separate evidence; this report only summarizes the current site's records and does not reuse historical US editorial conclusions.
